Theme 012 · Typography & graphic systems

Thermal Receipt

Pulse prints a running receipt of your product: a warm thermal strip feeds out of a little printer, line by line, with dotted leaders and a black-and-coral two-color print head. The feed stalls on the one line that is wrong, a coral circle lands around it, and a human ticks the box.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Paper strip — warm white, feed lines, edge shading for curl and a zig-zag tear at the bottom.
  • Line item — label · dotted leader · value in JetBrains Mono, 32–34 characters per line like a 58 mm roll.
  • Two-color head — black for normal lines, coral for the anomaly, the way two-color thermal paper prints.
  • Dithered header — the Acme mark pushed to one-bit with a halftone screen, plus double-height "ACME / PULSE".
  • Marker circle — one hand-drawn coral loop around the line that matters; never more than one per shot.
  • Printer body — dark device with a slot and a status LED that turns coral when the feed pauses.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Stepped feed — translateY one line per step (steps(1), 70 ms hold), one line per 16th note at 120 BPM (125 ms).
  • Print-head scan — each new line reveals with clip-path left → right in 90 ms, linear, so the feed sounds like the hi-hat.
  • Pause & tear — feed freezes for exactly one bar on the anomaly; the final tear slides up 20 px and rotates −4° (power3.out, 400 ms) on a downbeat.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

A receipt is a universal proof object: itemised, timestamped, final. It turns background monitoring into something you can literally hold. Risk: a tall strip fights a square frame; crop tight and never show more than about 12 lines.

Adapt to your product: print your own checks as line items (tests, invoices, sync jobs, API calls) and let only the failing one print in your accent color. The totals block is a natural place for your key number.
